subject: BrightGate discovery — model stability & next steps
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Park <oliver.park@brightgate.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-02T14:12:00Z
Subject: BrightGate discovery — model stability & next steps

Hi Oliver — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

1) Key takeaways from discovery
- Primary use case: automated triage + suggested responses for customer support tickets (English, short form).
- Target latency: <= 250ms p50 on 2k prompt length distribution; throughput ~ 40 req/sec for initial pilot.
- Data controls: must not retain raw tickets beyond processing window; audit logs required for compliance.

2) Recommended next items from Redwood
- Eval pack (attached): 250 representative tickets, baseline prompts, and expected labels.
- Recommended models: rdx-3b-ops (default low-cost baseline), rdx-7b-stable (recommended for quality).
- Prompt set: prompt_sets/brightgate_ticket_prompts_v1.txt attached. Use temp constraints for CSAT-sensitive responses.
- Benchmarks: preliminary results attached (benchmarks/brightgate_bench_v1.csv).

3) Risks and checks
- We flagged possible quality regression sensitivity for certain customer tone examples (see sample-cases in the eval pack). If you notice any output drift after model updates, we can pin to a specific model SHA or stage a rollback.

4) Next steps / asks
- Oliver: confirm a 1-week window to run the eval pack and whether BrightGate will provide masked production samples (preferable).
- Redwood (we): run evals, baseline dashboards, and propose a canary/pinning policy.
- Schedule a 30-min sync mid-next week to review results (proposed Wed 2027-05-11 16:00 ET).

Attachments: brightgate_eval_pack_v1.zip, prompt_sets/brightgate_ticket_prompts_v1.txt, benchmarks/brightgate_bench_v1.csv

Thanks — happy to adjust based on your timeline.

—
Grace O'Connor
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0118

From: Oliver Park <oliver.park@brightgate.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@brightgate.com
Date: 2027-05-02T18:03:00Z
Subject: Re: BrightGate discovery — model stability & next steps

Thanks Grace — this is helpful. We can share masked samples (I’ll send them to the Drive link) and run the eval pack next week. A couple of immediate concerns: 

- Our Security lead flagged that BrightGate can’t take on any latent regressions during the pilot window; they want a clear rollback/pinning SLA if a model update causes a material accuracy drop.
- On a related note: we had a small incident with another vendor last month where an open update changed responses for 8% of cases; we need to avoid surprises.

I also attached one failing example inline below that we noticed in another vendor test run — it’s the type of tone/intent mismatch we need to safeguard against.

--- example failing case ---
Ticket: “Customer says product crashed after update; upset and wants refund.”
Expected: empathy + clear next steps + escalation to billing if refund requested.
Observed (vendor A, after update): overly curt, omitted escalation.

Can Redwood commit to: 
1) A documented pin-to-version option available to us during the pilot window.
2) A runbook for quick rollback or emergency hold.

Oliver
Oliver Park
Head of Product Operations | BrightGate Solutions
oliver.park@brightgate.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Park <oliver.park@brightgate.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-02T20:45:00Z
Subject: Re: BrightGate discovery — model stability & next steps

Hi Oliver — quick technical reply on the rollback/pinning options and an operational proposal: 

1) Pinning options we can offer immediately
- Model pin: pin to a model artifact SHA (immutable) for the pilot; no automatic upgrades will be applied. This is the fastest option.
- Variant gating: route X% traffic to a stable variant while we run the new model on the rest; automatic fallback if quality drops > threshold.

2) Emergency path / runbook (summary)
- If BrightGate flags regression (via our eval dashboard or ticket): we’ll temporarily re-route traffic to the pinned SHA within 15 minutes for Dedicated and within 30 minutes for hosted tiers.
- We’ll provide a diff report (token-level and sample-level) within 4 hours for triage.
- If requested, we’ll roll back the model for the pilot window and freeze automated updates.

3) Suggested immediate tests we’ll run with your eval pack
- Regression delta: compare rdx-7b-stable@20270410 (baseline) vs rdx-7b-stable@20270501 (current) on the 250-ticket set; we’ll surface precision/recall on key intents and a tone consistency score.
- Canary: run a 10% traffic slow-roll with live logging for 48 hours and generate a stability report.

I’ve kickstarted the eval run; you’ll see an entry in the dashboard within ~8 hours: https://app.redwood.ai/evals/dashboard?account=BrightGate (linked in the eval pack).

Attachments in this reply: bench summary CSV (interim) and proposed rollback runbook (attached runbook_stub.pdf).

—
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Inference Reliability | Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Park <oliver.park@brightgate.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-03T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: BrightGate discovery — model stability & next steps

Oliver — appreciate the quick clarity. Confirming the plan so we all have the same timeline: 

1) BrightGate will drop masked production-like samples in the shared Drive by EOD 2027-05-03.
2) Redwood will run the eval pack and the regression delta (rdx-7b-stable@20270410 vs @20270501) and post interim results to the dashboard by 2027-05-03 20:00 ET.
3) If you spot any material regression in the interim report, Redwood will: 
   - Pin your pilot to the baseline SHA within 15 minutes (Dedicated) / 30 minutes (hosted).
   - Deliver a token/sample diff export and triage notes within 4 hours.
4) Schedule: 30-min sync to review final evals and canary plan on Tue 2027-05-11 16:00 ET. Meeting invite to follow.

We’ll also include a short suggested SLA paragraph for the pilot contract that captures the pin/rollback commitment — Vivek and Hannah will draft.

If that sounds good I’ll mark the HubSpot deal BG-2027-0421 with the pilot milestone and share access to the eval folder.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

—
Grace O'Connor
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
